criterion: conformance.report sorts Codex and hook sessions on one comparable value, and _overlaps needs no type filter to avoid inventing an overlap
summary: The reviewer's finding, fixed at the layer that owns it. Making Codex bounds comparable is correct; acting on them in _contested was not, because updated_at is when Codex last wrote the thread row rather than when the session ended. Every verdict now carries `bounds` - `observed` for a hook-watched session, `thread_lifetime` for one recovered from the store - and only observed windows take part in _contested. Four tests pin it, including the reviewer's own counter-example kept verbatim: a 23.6-day Codex window around a conformant session with its own edit record and graph transition, which must not be contested. The other three hold that two Codex rows do not contest each other, that two observed sessions still do - so the exclusion did not remove the case the flag exists for - and that every verdict says which kind of window it carries. Two guards: 'contested: only an observed window may contest' and 'contested: an observed window still contests another', both pinned. SCHEMA_VERSION is 3 and docs/conformance.md documents `bounds` and the restriction.
